name: 42212-sharedprefix-gptoss120b-2gpu
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3 on one a3 node (--gres=gpu:2), plus that node's host DRAM, which is where the 24 GiB KV tier declared in vllm-config.yaml lives.
parallelism: TP=2, PP=1, DP=1 -- one in-process vLLM engine over two GPUs, driven through guidellm's `vllm_python` backend, so there is no HTTP round trip.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), 8 streams, 480 requests, warmup 25% and cooldown 10% of completed requests (both `mode: requests`), 2400 s safety cap, static seed 42212.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn: 24 distinct 12288-token shared prefixes (one prefix bucket), plus 256 unique prompt tokens and exactly 64 output tokens per request (min = max on both). Prompt bodies are random text and nothing here reads them.
purpose: A document question-answering assistant on two GPUs, serving 8 concurrent users short answers over long shared document prefixes.
launch:
# The arguments the engine is launched with, on commit 02564b4de069a02d9f6abca57ebfd49115eaae39.
#
# FLAT YAML ONLY. A line beginning with a space is skipped, so a block-style mapping parses to
# nothing and the engine starts silently without it. `kv-transfer-config` below must stay on ONE
# LINE; a value beginning `{` is read as JSON.

model: openai/gpt-oss-120b
tensor-parallel-size: 2
max-model-len: 16384
block-size: 16

# `cpu_bytes_to_use` is 24 GiB AGGREGATE across ranks (the spec divides by world_size itself) and
# is hard-required: the spec raises at engine start when it is absent.
kv-transfer-config: {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"CPUOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":25769803776}}

# 6 GiB PER RANK, so 12 GiB of GPU KV across the two. Pinned rather than left to
# gpu-memory-utilization, which stays as the overall device budget.
kv-cache-memory-bytes: 6442450944
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.92

enable-prefix-caching: true
max-num-seqs: 32
max-num-batched-tokens: 16384
